results.answer: The AMF is an Access and Mobility Management Function. [1] The AMF should attempt to maintain support for emergency services and for MPS during an overload situation. [2] The AMF can either maintain support for emergency services and for MPS or not during an overload situation when recovering. [3] The AMF shall provide the 5G - AN node with the weight factors for each TNL association of the AMF. [4] The AMF shall be able to request the 5G - AN node to add or remove TNL associations to the AMF. [5] The AMF shall be able to indicate to the 5G - AN node the set of TNL associations used for UE-associated signalling and the set of TNL associations used for non-UE associated signalling. [6]

results.answer: The 5GC supports two possible deployments scenarios for a PDU Session in the case of roaming: Local Break Out (LBO) and Home Routed (HR). [1] In the Local Break Out (LBO) scenario, the SMF and all UPF(s) involved by the PDU Session are under control of the VPLMN. [2] In the Home Routed (HR) scenario, the PDU Session is supported by a SMF function under control of the HPLMN, by a SMF function under control of the VPLMN, by at least one UPF under control of the HPLMN and by at least one UPF under control of the VPLMN. [3] The Home Routed roaming scenario is supported for 5G-RG connected via NG-RAN, while Local Breakout scenario is not supported. [4]
